content: In similar studies conducted on BALB/c mice and in two-year studies on Wistar rats, there was no evidence of mutagenicity observed. This was consistent across both prokaryotic organisms, such as Salmonella typhi and Escherichia coli, and eukaryotic organisms, including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Drosophila melanogaster, and ICR/Ha Swiss mice. However, an increase in chromatid breaks was noted when whole blood cell cultures were treated with rifampin. Additionally, an increased frequency of chromosomal aberrations was observed in vitro in lymphocytes obtained from patients treated with combinations of rifampin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide, as well as combinations of streptomycin, rifampin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide. Clinical Studies There is limited information available regarding clinical studies of oral rifampin in the drug label. How Supplied Rifampin capsules, USP, are available in the following forms: 150 mg opaque orange capsules, printed in white with “Rifampin 150” on one half and “VP/015” on the other half: Bottles of 30 (NDC 61748-015-30) Unit dose boxes of 100 (NDC 61748-015-11) 300 mg opaque orange capsules, printed in white with “Rifampin 300” on one half and “VP/018” on the other half: Bottles of 30 (NDC 61748-018-30) Bottles of 60 (NDC 61748-018-60) Bottles of 100 (NDC 61748-018-01) Unit dose boxes of 100 (NDC 61748-018-11) Storage Rifampin should be stored at 20–25°C (68–77°F) in a dry place. Avoid excessive heat and protect the medication from light. Dispense in a tight, light-resistant container as defined in the USP, using a child-resistant closure. Patient Counseling Information Patients should be informed that antibacterial drugs, including rifampin, should only be used to treat bacterial infections. They should not be used to treat viral infections, such as the common cold. When rifampin is prescribed for a bacterial infection, patients should be advised that although they may feel better early in the course of therapy, the medication must be taken exactly as directed. Skipping doses or failing to complete the full course of therapy may: 1. Decrease the effectiveness of the immediate treatment. 2. Increase the likelihood that bacteria will develop resistance, rendering rifampin or other antibacterial drugs ineffective in the future. Patients should be informed that rifampin may cause a reddish discoloration of urine, sweat, sputum, and tears. They should be forewarned about this effect, as soft contact lenses may become permanently stained. Patients should also be advised that the reliability of oral or other systemic hormonal contraceptives may be affected, and alternative contraceptive measures should be considered. Patients should take rifampin either 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal with a full glass of water. They should promptly notify their physician if they experience any of the following symptoms: fever, loss of appetite, malaise, nausea and vomiting, darkened urine, yellowish discoloration of the skin and eyes, or pain or swelling of the joints. Compliance with the full course of therapy must be emphasized, and the importance of not missing any doses should be stressed. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and oral rifampin has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Brand Names Rifadin Rimactane Look-Alike Drug Names There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for oral rifampin in the drug label.
